Here is a Lean4 proof of the normality of the Champernowne sequence to any base b > 1:
https://github.com/OldMathematician/ChampernowneNormality

See Champernowne's original paper:
D. G. Champernowne, "The Construction of Decimals Normal in the Scale of Ten," Journal of the London Mathematical Society, vol. 8, no. 4 (1933), pp. 254–260. doi:10.1112/jlms/s1-8.4.254

The code was developed using Claude Code.

Note: I am Arthur Champernowne, David's son.

Congrats! I don't really understand the proof :sweat_smile: but in general to make people take AI-generated proofs seriously, you'd want to set up your repo with https://github.com/leanprover/comparator using a Challenge.lean and Solution.lean pattern (e.g. this repo). For your case in particular, I'm not sure how hard it is to put all the required definitions into one single file though.
This topic was moved here from #general > Champernowne Sequence Normality Proof by Matthew Ballard.
